findings.claim: The productive asset base is 845,256 bitcoin, 4.025% of all bitcoin that will ever exist, worth $65.08bn at $77,000. It is 94.3% of gross assets of $68.98bn. The next largest corporate holders are Twenty One Capital at 43,500 BTC, Metaplanet at 40,177 and MARA at 35,303.
findings.label: FACT
findings.source: Strategy holdings after the 2026-08-31 purchase; bitcoin treasury trackers, September 2026; bitcoin price 2026-09-11

findings.claim: The accumulation engine switched off in mid-June 2026. Holdings went from 762,099 BTC at 2026-03-31 to 843,775 at 2026-06-30 (+81,676 in the quarter, +11%), then to 845,256 at 2026-08-31 - just 1,481 bitcoin in two months, a 98% collapse in the accumulation rate, coinciding exactly with mNAV crossing below 1.0.
findings.label: FACT
findings.source: Q1 2026 holdings market value of $51.6bn at 2026-03-31; Q2 2026 results; holdings disclosure after the 2026-08-31 purchase of 4,600 BTC at an average $80,318

findings.claim: The annual cash carry of the capital structure is approximately $1,633m: $1,603m of preferred dividends (annualising Q2's $400.7m) plus roughly $30m of convertible interest on $6.70bn of 0%-2.25% notes. That is $1,932 per bitcoin per year, or 2.51% of the bitcoin stack.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived from Q2 2026 preferred dividends of $400.7m, the $6.70bn convertible balance at 2026-06-30 and note coupons of 0%-2.25%, divided by 845,256 BTC at $77,000

findings.claim: Strategy's carrying cost is roughly 12.5x the approximately 0.20% annual fee on a US spot bitcoin ETF - an identical exposure available to any buyer. The wrapper's competitive position deteriorated for reasons entirely outside management's control when the spot ETFs launched.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.unit: x the cost of a spot bitcoin ETF
findings.source: Derived: 2.51% carrying cost against a typical US spot bitcoin ETF expense ratio of about 0.20%

findings.claim: The funding mix shifted the wrong way: from roughly $7bn of convertible notes at a blended ~0.4% in 2024 to $6.70bn of convertibles plus about $14.80bn of perpetual preferred at a blended ~10.8% today, taking annual carry from approximately nothing to $1.63bn in about two years.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived from the preferred stack (STRC 12%, STRF 10%, STRD 10%, STRE ~10%, STRK 8%) weighted by estimated balances; convertible balance $6.70bn at 2026-06-30. The 2024 base is unsourced and the comparison is stated conservatively

findings.claim: The carry is procyclical: at a constant $1.633bn of cash obligations it is 1.61% of the stack at bitcoin $120,000, 2.51% at $77,000, 4.29% at $45,000 and 6.44% at $30,000 - and the STRC ratchet raises the numerator in exactly the states where the denominator is falling.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived at a constant $1.633bn cash carry across bitcoin prices; conservative because the STRC ratchet raises the carry as the price falls

findings.claim: The USD reserve of $2.40bn covers roughly 17.6 months of the $1.633bn annual cash carry with zero new issuance. S&P's B- rating explicitly cites low US dollar liquidity as a rating constraint.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.unit: months of carry covered by the USD reserve
findings.source: Derived from the 2026-06-30 USD reserve (cash $1.71bn plus short-term investments $0.74bn) against the derived annual carry; S&P Global Ratings, 2025-10-27

findings.claim: A 24-month closed capital-markets window costs about 42,400 bitcoin (5.0% of the stack) if bitcoin holds at $77,000, 65,400 (7.7%) at $50,000, and roughly 98,700 (11.7%) at $35,000 with two ratchet triggers - because the numerator rises as the denominator falls.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived from the annual cash carry across bitcoin price scenarios, assuming the USD reserve is preserved

findings.claim: Unlike a GPU fleet or a utility rate base, bitcoin has no depreciation, no maintenance capex and effectively no operating cost - 100% of capital deployed still exists and still works. The offset is that it produces no cash flow, so 100% of the cost of owning it is financing cost, which must be paid from a $495m software business and the asset itself.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Structural assessment of the asset versus regulated and technology comparators; software revenue per Q1 and Q2 2026 results

findings.claim: One hundred percent of bitcoin purchases are growth capex and none is maintenance. There is no sustaining spend that can be cut in a downturn to preserve cash; the only cuttable line is the purchase programme, and it has already been cut to zero.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Structural conclusion from the asset's zero-maintenance character and the observed purchase pause of mid-June to 2026-08-31

risks.text: The carry is procyclical: a falling bitcoin price mechanically raises the cost of carrying bitcoin as a percentage of the stack, and the STRC ratchet raises the dollar obligation in the same states
A 24-month closed issuance window consumes 5% of the bitcoin stack if the price holds and nearly 12% if it halves
The wrapper costs 12.5x a spot bitcoin ETF for identical underlying exposure, a competitive disadvantage that did not exist when the strategy was designed and cannot be reversed
There is no maintenance spend to cut in a downturn - the only cuttable line is the purchase programme, which is already at zero
845,256 BTC is 4.025% of total supply; there is no orderly path to liquidating it if one were ever required

Q3 2026 results: bitcoin marked at quarter end, USD reserve balance, and the scale of dividend-funded bitcoin sales
STRC returning to or above its $100 stated amount, reopening the preferred ATM on non-punitive terms
A further convertible repurchase at a discount - the only demonstrably accretive capital action taken in 2026

conclusions: The productive asset is 845,256 bitcoin, 4.025% of total supply, held at an average cost of $75,417 against about $77,000. The entire six-year programme sits 2.1% above water and was below it at the last quarter end.
The accumulation engine switched off in mid-June 2026: +81,676 BTC in Q2, then +1,481 in two months, a 98% collapse coinciding exactly with mNAV crossing below 1.0.
The unit cost of this asset is financial carry: $1,932 per bitcoin per year, 2.51% of the stack, roughly 12.5 times the fee on a spot bitcoin ETF offering identical exposure.
The funding mix shifted the wrong way - from roughly $7bn of ~0.4% convertibles to about $14.8bn of ~10.8% perpetual preferred - taking annual carry from nearly nothing to $1.63bn in two years.
The carry is procyclical by construction: 2.51% of the stack at $77,000, 4.29% at $45,000, 6.44% at $30,000, with the STRC ratchet adding to the obligation in exactly those states.

The asset itself is excellent on the tests this protocol usually applies - no depreciation, no maintenance, no operating cost - and that advantage is neutralised by the fact that it yields nothing while the liabilities funding it yield 10.8%.
thesisImpact: Prices what it costs to wait for the Phase 1 mechanism to restart: 2.51% of the bitcoin stack per year, rising as the price falls, with no operating asset capable of covering it. Sets up Phase 3's question directly - with the equity ATM shut, where does $1.633bn a year actually come from?
